title: Spillovers from Online Engagement: How a Newspaper Subscriber's Activation of Digital Paywall Access Affects Her Retention and Subscription Revenue
eligible_reason: Staggered binary design: after_activation switches on in the week a print subscriber activates digital paywall access (53 weekly activation cohorts in the shipped sample), with coarsened-exact-matched non-activators (never treated) assigned to each activator's matching cohort. Main specifications are linear subscriber-week regressions with subscriber FE and matching-cohort x week FE, no covariates, clustered by subscriber (Table 3 col 2, Table 4 col 1, Table 6, Figures 4-5). Each subscriber belongs to exactly one cohort (no duplication), so cohort x week is a time-invariant group x time FE, following the mnsc.2022.03770 precedent (batch_id#dte). Table 7 (Oster test) also reports a plain TWFE with subscriber and week FE only.
design_notes: replication.do. Replication_Tables2thru7.csv: 1,434 subscribers (728 activators, 706 controls) x 213 weeks (305,391 rows, near-balanced), cohort_id = activation week of the cohort's activator(s) (53 values, 364-728 in steps of 7), activation_week missing for controls, after_activation = 1(week_id >= cohort_id) for activators. Event-time dummies b10..b2, a0..a10 (b1 omitted; b10 bins rel <= -10, a10 bins rel >= 10; a10 is also 1 for every control row, which subscriber FE absorb). Table 3 col 1, 3, 4 are Cox models (stcox, strata cohort_id); Table 4 col 2 is a causal forest (grf), col 3 gsynth; Table 5 collapses to pre/post with a selection residual; Table 7 also has Rosenbaum bounds (psmatch2); Table 8 regresses forest effects on characteristics. Full-data log: Table 3 col 2 -0.0646 (0.0034); Table 4 col 1 0.4308 (0.0230), N = 5,993,302, 28,144 subscribers; Table 6 six-month window 0.2671 (0.0148), placebo 0.0002 (0.0052), one-year window 0.3144 (0.0172), placebo 0.0141 (0.0066); Table 7 plain TWFE 0.3547 (0.0201).
n_eligible_specs_note: Table 3 col 2 (former, static), Figure 4 (former, event study), Table 4 col 1 (price, static), Figure 5 (price, event study), Table 6 six-month window, Table 6 six-month fake-date placebo, Table 6 one-year window, Table 6 one-year fake-date placebo, Table 7 plain TWFE (subscriber + week FE). 7 if the two fake-date placebos are dropped; Table 7 TWFE counts only if its coefficient is printed in the article table.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 53 weekly activation cohorts (week_id 364-728) in the shipped 5% sample, 3-25 activators each; full data 28,144 subscribers.

specs.treatment_definition: 1 from the subscriber's digital-paywall activation week onward (activation_week = cohort_id for activators; missing for CEM-matched non-activators, who are never treated)
specs.reported_location: Table 7 (Oster/psacalc 'controlled' regression; confirm the coefficient is printed)
specs.notes: Plain staggered TWFE where activator cohorts act as controls for each other; most informative for negative weights.

data_files_note: readme.pdf: 'the replication data are a random sample of the full data with anonymized ID's. Because of this, replication results will differ slightly from those reported in the paper.' Shipped panel has 1,434 of 28,144 subscribers (about 5%). gsynth data not shipped.
software_notes: Stata reghdfe/areg/stcox/psmatch2/psacalc; R grf and gsynth.
priority_note: Eligible on real random-subsample data; published estimates are full-sample, so replication is approximate.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. FLAGS FOR LEAD: (1) cohort_id equals the activator's activation week, so cohort x week FE make every comparison within a single-date cohort (no forbidden comparisons); I followed the mnsc.2022.03770 precedent (eligible), but mnsc.2021.03884 called a matched-cohort x time FE design stacked. Under the stacked reading only the Table 7 plain TWFE (1 spec) qualifies. (2) Two Table 6 specs are fake-date placebos. (3) Random 5% subsample: expect approximate replication; small cohorts (3-25 activators) in the shipped data.
